Resistor.description: Passive component that limits current flow
steps: Power off the circuit completely
Set multimeter to Resistance (Ω) mode
Select appropriate range (e.g., 20kΩ for a 10kΩ resistor)
Disconnect at least one resistor lead from the circuit
Touch red probe to one lead, black probe to the other
Read the measured resistance value
Resistor.expected: Within ±5% of nominal value printed on component
bad_conditions: Reading shows OL (open circuit) — resistor is broken internally
Reading shows 0Ω (short circuit) — resistor is shorted
Reading deviates more than 20% from nominal — degraded
Resistor.repair: Replace with same resistance value and wattage rating

steps: Power off and discharge the circuit (short leads briefly)
Set multimeter to Capacitance mode (F symbol)
Disconnect capacitor from circuit
For polarised capacitors: red probe to positive (+) lead
Touch probes to capacitor leads
Wait for stable reading
bad_conditions: Reading shows OL — capacitor is open
Reading shows 0 — capacitor is shorted
Physical signs: bulging top, leaked electrolyte
Capacitor.repair: Replace with same capacitance, voltage rating, and polarity type

Diode.description: Allows current flow in one direction only
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Diode test mode (diode symbol)
Touch red probe to anode (+), black probe to cathode (-)
Read forward voltage drop
Reverse probes and check reverse reading
bad_conditions: Forward reads OL — diode is open (broken)
Both directions read 0 — diode is shorted
Reverse conducts — diode is leaking
Diode.repair: Replace with same type and voltage/current rating

Zener_Diode.description: Diode that regulates voltage by conducting in reverse at zener voltage
Zener_Diode.test_method: Diode test mode (forward direction same as regular diode)
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Diode test mode
Test forward direction: red to anode, black to cathode
Read forward voltage drop
Note: zener voltage requires special test circuit to verify
Zener_Diode.expected: Forward: 0.5–0.7V (same as silicon diode in forward direction)
Zener_Diode.good_condition: Forward voltage 0.6–0.7V; reverse reads OL in diode mode
bad_conditions: Forward reads OL — zener is open
Both directions conduct — zener is shorted
Zener_Diode.repair: Replace with same zener voltage and power rating

Transistor.description: Semiconductor device for amplification or switching
Transistor.test_method: Diode test mode on each junction
steps: Power off the circuit
Identify pins: Base (B), Collector (C), Emitter (E)
Set multimeter to Diode test mode
For NPN: red probe to Base, black to Emitter — expect 0.6–0.7V
Red probe to Base, black to Collector — expect 0.6–0.7V
All other combinations should read OL
Transistor.expected: B-E junction: 0.6–0.7V forward. B-C junction: 0.6–0.7V forward. All reverse: OL
Transistor.good_condition: Both junctions show proper diode behaviour
bad_conditions: Any junction reads 0 — junction is shorted
Any junction reads OL forward — junction is open
C-E reads conductive — transistor is shorted
Transistor.repair: Replace with same transistor type (NPN/PNP) and specifications

MOSFET.description: Field-effect transistor controlled by gate voltage
MOSFET.test_method: Diode test mode on body diode
steps: Power off the circuit
Identify pins: Gate (G), Drain (D), Source (S)
Set multimeter to Diode test mode
For N-channel: red probe to Source, black to Drain — expect 0.4–0.6V
Reverse should read OL
Gate to Source/Drain should read OL in both directions
MOSFET.expected: Source-Drain body diode: 0.4–0.6V forward, OL reverse. Gate: OL both ways
MOSFET.good_condition: Body diode intact, gate properly isolated
bad_conditions: D-S reads 0 in both directions — MOSFET shorted
Gate conducts — gate oxide breakdown
MOSFET.repair: Replace with same type, voltage, and current rating

IC.description: Integrated circuit containing multiple electronic functions
steps: Power off the circuit
Visually inspect for burn marks, cracked package, bent pins
Set multimeter to DC Voltage mode
Power on the circuit carefully
Measure VCC pin to GND — should match rated supply voltage
Measure GND pin — should read 0V
IC.expected: Supply voltage within ±10% of rated value (e.g., 4.5–5.5V for 5V IC)
IC.good_condition: Correct supply voltage present, no visible damage
bad_conditions: IC is hot to touch — excessive current draw
Supply voltage absent or wrong — power delivery issue
Visible burn marks — IC failed
IC.repair: Replace with exact IC part number; check surrounding circuit for root cause

LED.description: Light Emitting Diode — produces light when forward biased
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Diode test mode
Touch red probe to anode (+, longer lead), black to cathode (-)
LED should glow faintly in diode test mode
Read forward voltage
Reverse probes — should read OL
LED.good_condition: Correct forward voltage and LED glows during test
bad_conditions: No glow and OL reading — LED is open
Reads 0 forward — LED is shorted
Wrong forward voltage — LED degraded
LED.repair: Replace with same colour, forward voltage, and current rating

Inductor.description: Coil that stores energy in magnetic field and resists current changes
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to low Resistance mode (200Ω range)
Disconnect inductor from circuit if possible
Touch probes to both inductor leads
Read DC resistance of winding
Inductor.expected: Very low resistance (typically 0.1–50Ω depending on inductor type)
Inductor.good_condition: Low DC resistance reading — winding intact
bad_conditions: OL reading — winding is open (broken coil)
Higher than expected resistance — partial winding damage
Inductor.repair: Replace with same inductance value and current rating

Fuse.description: Overcurrent protection device that breaks circuit when current exceeds rating
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Continuity mode (beep symbol) or low Ω range
Touch probes to both fuse terminals
Listen for beep (continuity mode) or read resistance
Fuse.expected: Good fuse: continuity beep or near 0Ω. Blown fuse: OL (open circuit)
bad_conditions: OL or no beep — fuse is blown
Visually check for broken wire or blackening inside glass fuse
Fuse.repair: Replace with EXACT same current rating and type. Investigate why fuse blew before replacement.

Connector.description: Mechanical interface for connecting/disconnecting electrical circuits
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Continuity mode
Test each pin from connector entry to PCB pad
Check for bent, corroded, or missing pins visually
Connector.expected: Each pin shows continuity from plug to socket; no cross-connections between pins
Connector.good_condition: All pins show continuity; no shorts between adjacent pins
bad_conditions: OL on a pin — broken or dirty contact
Beep between adjacent pins — short circuit in connector
Connector.repair: Clean with contact cleaner; replace connector if pins are bent or broken

Jumper.description: Short-circuit connector used to configure circuit options
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Continuity mode
Touch probes to both jumper pins
Should beep if jumper cap is installed
Jumper.expected: Continuity when jumper cap installed; open circuit when removed
Jumper.good_condition: Correct continuity based on jumper cap presence
bad_conditions: No continuity with cap installed — bad jumper cap or corroded pins
Jumper.repair: Replace jumper cap or clean pins with contact cleaner

Switch.description: Mechanical device to open or close a circuit
Switch.test_method: Continuity test in both switch positions
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to Continuity mode
Test switch in OFF position — should read OL (no beep)
Activate switch to ON position
Test again — should read continuity (beep)
Switch.good_condition: Clear switching between open and closed states
bad_conditions: Always OL — switch contacts corroded or broken
Always continuity — switch shorted internally
Switch.repair: Clean with contact cleaner; replace switch if mechanism is broken

Transformer.description: Transfers electrical energy between circuits via magnetic coupling
Transformer.test_method: Winding resistance test on primary and secondary
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to low Resistance mode
Test primary winding: touch probes to primary input pins
Test secondary winding: touch probes to secondary output pins
Both should show low resistance
Transformer.expected: Primary and secondary windings both show low resistance (typically 1–100Ω)
Transformer.good_condition: Both windings show low, measurable resistance
bad_conditions: OL on any winding — winding is open (broken)
0Ω on winding — winding is shorted
Burning smell — insulation breakdown
Transformer.repair: Replace transformer with same specifications (voltage ratio, current rating)

Potentiometer.test_method: Resistance measurement across wiper and ends
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to appropriate Resistance range
Measure end-to-end resistance (pins 1 to 3) — should equal rated value
Measure pin 1 to wiper (pin 2) while rotating
Measure pin 2 to pin 3 while rotating
Both should change smoothly without jumps
Potentiometer.expected: End-to-end = rated value. Wiper readings vary smoothly 0 to rated value
Potentiometer.good_condition: Smooth, continuous resistance change across full rotation
bad_conditions: Scratchy or jumping readings — dirty or worn track
OL end-to-end — resistive track broken
Wiper reads OL at some positions — open track
Potentiometer.repair: Clean with contact cleaner; replace if track is worn

MOV.description: Metal Oxide Varistor — protects circuit from voltage spikes
MOV.test_method: Resistance test (high resistance expected in normal state)
steps: Power off the circuit
Set multimeter to high Resistance range (20MΩ if available)
Touch probes to both MOV leads
Read resistance in normal (non-conducting) state
MOV.expected: Very high resistance (>1MΩ) in normal state — MOV not conducting
MOV.good_condition: Very high resistance indicates MOV is intact
bad_conditions: Low resistance or near 0Ω — MOV has clamped and failed short
Visible cracking or burn marks — MOV absorbed a surge and failed
OL is also acceptable (some MOVs read OL when healthy)
MOV.repair: Replace with same varistor voltage (Vnom) and energy rating. Check power supply for surge source.
